response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile senior engineer with genuine developer-tooling credentials (C/C++ work on the LabWindows/CVI IDE, custom test runner and assertion libraries in D, CI/CD infrastructure), but the core requirements of this role are not met. The JD demands strong Java and Kotlin with deep JVM understanding plus solid Spring/Quarkus/Hibernate experience; the resume shows Java only as a listed skill and in passing (robotic arms, device orchestration tooling ~2016-2018), no Kotlin at all, and no enterprise JVM framework, build-tool, or application-server experience. The last decade is dominated by TypeScript/Node.js, D, and web/cloud work. Ramp-up on the enterprise JVM ecosystem would be substantial for a mid-senior IC expected to own subsystems end-to-end.
strengths: Real IDE/developer-tooling experience (NI LabWindows/CVI, test runner and assertion libraries, MCP code generators)
Long senior-level track record across backend, low-latency systems, and full-stack product work
Strong engineering-craft signals: TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development, open-source ownership, teaching/talks
concerns: No demonstrated Kotlin experience and only shallow, dated Java exposure
No Spring, Quarkus, Hibernate, Gradle/Maven, or application-server work anywhere in the resume
Recent 8+ years centered on TypeScript/Node and D rather than large-scale JVM codebases
